source.title: Non-elliptic Shimura curves of genus one
source.journal: Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 58(4) (2006), 927-948

locators.explicit_models: Table 2, p939 (PDF page 13), four rows D=210, m=30,42,70,105
locators.canonical_model_convention: Theorem 5.1 and following paragraph, p940 (PDF page 14)

applications.result: Exact four rational quotient curves, not merely isogenous Jacobians
applications.hypotheses: D=210 is a product of four distinct primes; N=1; each m=30,42,70,105 is a positive divisor of D listed in Lemma 4.1

applications.result: The labeled quotient Jacobians have the four required j invariants
applications.method: Exact arithmetic using Table 2 binary quartic invariants, cross-checked against Table 3 short-Weierstrass equations

applications.result: X/W has five rational branch points with inertia labels 30,42,70,105,210
applications.method: Genus formula, characteristic-zero cyclic stabilizers, Riemann-Hurwitz, and abelian inertia product relation
Full two-torsion translation quotient preserves the elliptic j invariant; exact 36-pair cross-ratio enumeration

scope: Closes only the quotient-identification input Q and its exact branch configuration. Does not certify the separate field-degree, integral-model, Hodge-comparison, or non-CM height arguments.
replaced_source: Padurariu-Saia arXiv:2509.25368 and quotient-models.m are no longer needed for Q. No isomorphism between their large quartics and the 2006 models is asserted or needed.
